Feature: Payer column shows correct party for credit (incoming) transactions
Test Steps:
1. Find any credit (In) transaction in the table
2. Look at the Payer column
Expected Result: Payer column shows the other_party name (the external sender). Company name (BluePine) appears in Recipient column.

Feature: Recipient column shows correct party for debit (outgoing) transactions
Test Steps:
1. Find any debit (Out) transaction in the table
2. Look at the Recipient column
Expected Result: Recipient column shows the other_party name (external receiver). Company name (BluePine) appears in Payer column.

Feature: Long party names are truncated with tooltip
Precondition: A transaction with a long other_party name exists
Test Steps:
1. Find a transaction with a long Payer or Recipient name
2. Hover over the truncated text
Expected Result: Full name appears in the browser tooltip (title attribute). Row does not break layout.

Test Steps: 1. Look at the table headers
Expected Result: Category column header is indigo/purple to distinguish it from the grey headers of other columns.

Feature: Category cell shows placeholder when unset
Test Steps:
1. Find an unclassified transaction
2. Look at the Category column
Expected Result: Shows a faint placeholder (e.g. "Category") not a blank or broken cell.

Feature: Category cell shows current value when set
Precondition: Transaction with a category already set
Test Steps:
1. Find a classified transaction
2. Look at the Category column
Expected Result: Displays the category value as a chip/badge. Color-coded if applicable.

Test Steps: 1. Click the Category cell on any row
Expected Result: A dropdown appears with the list of available categories. Closes on outside click.

Feature: Dropdown has a search/filter input when many options exist
Precondition: Rules table has more than 6 categories
Test Steps:
1. Click any Category cell
2. Look at the dropdown
Expected Result: A search input appears at the top of the dropdown. Typing filters the option list in real time.

Feature: Selecting a category closes the dropdown and updates the row
Test Steps:
1. Click Category cell
2. Select any option from the dropdown
Expected Result: Dropdown closes. Row immediately shows the selected category without page reload.

Test Steps:
1. Click Category cell on a classified transaction
2. Look for a clear option at the bottom
Expected Result: A "✕ Clear category" button appears. Clicking it removes the category and sets the cell back to placeholder.

Feature: Credit transactions show green In badge
Test Steps: 1. Find a credit (incoming) transaction
Expected Result: In/Out column shows a green badge with an arrow-down-left icon and "In" label.

Feature: Debit transactions show red Out badge
Test Steps: 1. Find a debit (outgoing) transaction
Expected Result: In/Out column shows a red badge with an arrow-up-right icon and "Out" label.

Test Steps: 1. Look at the Total Amount column for a credit row
Expected Result: Amount is formatted in green (e.g. +48,500 USD).

Test Steps: 1. Look at the Total Amount column for a debit row
Expected Result: Amount is formatted in red with parentheses or minus (e.g. (12,800 USD)).

Feature: Sort by Date ascending and descending
Test Steps:
1. Click the Date column header once
2. Click again to reverse
Expected Result: Transactions reorder. Sort icon updates (up/down arrow). Clicking a third time resets.

Test Steps: 1. Click the Total Amount column header
Expected Result: Transactions sort by amount ascending, then descending on second click.

Test Steps:
1. Apply date range and company filter
2. Look at the 4 summary cards above the table
Expected Result: Cards show: Money In (green), Money Out (red), Net Change (green/red), Transaction Count — all matching the filtered results.

Test Steps:
1. Select a specific company from the company dropdown
2. Apply filter
Expected Result: Only transactions for that company appear. Summary cards update accordingly.

Feature: Search filters by party name or reference
Test Steps: 1. Type a vendor name (e.g. "Amazon") in the search box
Expected Result: Table shows only transactions where other_party or reference contains the search string.

Test Steps: 1. Select EUR from the currency dropdown
Expected Result: Only EUR transactions shown. USD/GBP rows disappear.

Test Steps:
1. Select "In" from the type filter
2. Then try "Out"
Expected Result: Only credit or debit transactions shown respectively.

Feature: Export CSV contains Payer and Recipient columns
Test Steps:
1. Apply any filter
2. Click Export CSV button
3. Open the downloaded file
Expected Result: CSV file includes columns: Date, Payer, Recipient, Currency, Category, Total Amount, In/Out — matching what is visible on screen.

Test Steps:
1. Look at the pagination bar below the table
2. Click Next page
Expected Result: Table advances to the next page. Previous/next buttons update correctly. Page count shown.

Test Steps:
1. Open sidebar Settings section
2. Look for "Accounting Categories" menu item
Expected Result: Menu item appears with tag icon. Clicking it opens the rules table.

Test Steps: 1. Open sidebar Settings section
Expected Result: Accounting Categories menu item is NOT visible to non-Admin users.

Test Steps: 1. Navigate to Settings → Accounting Categories
Expected Result: Table shows all rules with columns: Payer, Recipient, Account/Wallet, Category.

Test Steps:

2. Click Save
Expected Result: New row appears in the table. Success toast shown. Row persists after page refresh.

Precondition: At least one rule in the table
Test Steps:
1. Hover over a row — pencil icon appears
2. Click pencil to enter edit mode
3. Change Category field value
4. Click Save
Expected Result: Row updates in place. New category value is visible. No page reload needed.

Precondition: At least one rule in the table
Test Steps:
1. Hover over a row
2. Click the trash icon
Expected Result: Row is removed from table immediately. Does not reappear on refresh.

Test Steps:
1. Click Upload CSV
2. Select a valid CSV file with columns: payer,recipient,account_wallet,category
3. Submit
Expected Result: All rules from CSV are loaded into the table. Previous rules are replaced. Success message shown.

Test Steps: 1. Attempt upload of CSV missing required columns
Expected Result: Error message shown. Table is not cleared or corrupted.

Feature: Dropdown shows live options from rules table
Test Steps:
1. Open Transactions page
2. Click the Category cell on any transaction
Expected Result: Dropdown options match the unique categories from vendor_classification_rules table (not a hardcoded static list).

Feature: Dropdown falls back to built-in list when rules table is empty
Test Steps:
1. Open Transactions page
2. Click any Category cell
Expected Result: Dropdown still shows the fallback category list. No blank or broken dropdown.

Feature: PATCH endpoint accepts CSV-format categories (e.g. INC_Client Deposit)
Test Steps: 1. PATCH /api/transactions/:id/classify with { "category": "INC_Client Deposit" }
Expected Result: 200 OK. Category set. No 400 error about invalid category.

Test Steps: 1. PATCH /api/transactions/:id/classify with { "geo": "INVALID" }
Expected Result: 400 error returned. Transaction not updated.

Feature: Category written to DB — persists on refresh
Test Steps:
1. Select a category
2. Refresh the full page
3. Find the same transaction
Expected Result: Category value still shows — confirmed persisted to wallet_transactions table.

Feature: Setting a category auto-creates a rule if none exists
Precondition: Transaction payer+recipient NOT in rules table
Test Steps:
1. Manually set a category on that transaction
2. Navigate to Settings → Accounting Categories
Expected Result: A new rule appears with the transaction's payer + recipient + the chosen category.

Feature: Does NOT create duplicate rule when one already exists
Precondition: Rule already exists for that payer+recipient
Test Steps:
1. Manually set a category on a transaction whose payer+recipient already has a rule
2. Check vendor_classification_rules
Expected Result: No duplicate row created. Existing rule untouched.

Test Steps:
1. Manually classify a credit transaction
2. Check auto-created rule
Expected Result: Rule payer = other_party (external sender), Rule recipient = company name.

Test Steps:
1. Manually classify a debit transaction
2. Check auto-created rule
Expected Result: Rule payer = company name, Rule recipient = other_party (external receiver).

Precondition: A rule exists for the vendor
Test Steps:
1. Trigger sync
2. Check the transaction
Expected Result: Category is set automatically from the matching rule.

Feature: Auto-classifier does NOT overwrite manually set category
Precondition: Transaction already has a manual category
Test Steps: 1. Trigger sync again
Expected Result: Category is unchanged — WHERE category IS NULL OR category = '' guard works.

Feature: Unclassified transaction triggers Zapier email alert
Test Steps:
1. Trigger sync with a transaction that has no matching rule
2. Check email inbox
Expected Result: Zapier email alert received with transaction details and AI-suggested category.

Expected Result: Transaction classified correctly. Alias map + lowercasing resolves the variation.
